learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the powerful concept of 'Similarity' in geometry, master the Basic Proportionality Theorem, and learn criteria to prove triangles similar!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Congruent figures have the exact same shape AND size (like a photocopy). Similar figures have the same shape but NOT necessarily the same size (like zooming in on a photo).
Two polygons are similar if: 1. Their corresponding angles are equal, AND 2. The lengths of their corresponding sides are in the same ratio (proportion).
If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, then the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. (If DE || BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC).
You don't need to check all angles and sides. Use these shortcuts: AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle), SSS (Side-Side-Side Proportional), or SAS (Side-Angle-Side Proportional).

fun_activity.title: ☀️ Shadow Geometry
fun_activity.instructions: Stand outside on a sunny day next to a tall tree. The ratio of your height to your shadow's length is identical to the ratio of the tree's height to the tree's shadow. This is because the sun's rays form 'Similar Triangles'!

exam_tips: 📌 The proof of the Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT) is one of the most frequently asked 5-mark questions. Practice drawing the construction and writing the steps clearly.
📌 When writing that two triangles are similar (e.g., ΔABC ~ ΔPQR), the order of the letters matters immensely! A corresponds to P, B to Q, and C to R.
📌 If two angles of a triangle are equal to two angles of another (AA criterion), the third angle is automatically equal, making them similar.
quick_recap: ⭐ All congruent figures are similar, but similar figures are not necessarily congruent.
⭐ All regular polygons (like equilateral triangles or squares) with the same number of sides are always similar.
⭐ The BPT also has a converse: If a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it must be parallel to the third side.
